newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 9.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Pricing policies for the supply of natural gas will be based on regional requirements, in accordance with a bill submitted to Parliament yesterday by Development Minister Vasso Papandreou. The bill paves the way for the calling of an international tender for the participation of the private sector in the distribution of natural gas.
--Payment rates for jointly-financed projects in the programme for public investments have taken off in the first half-year, compared to last year, increasing by 95.8 percent.

--A wide-ranging meeting with the participation of all economic and finance ministers has been scheduled for July 15. The focus of the meeting will be the taking of further anti-inflationary measures as well as the better coordination of work amongst the government's economic team. Also to be discussed: the recently released Spraos report on convergence; the possibility of reduced corporate taxation; and a freeze on price increases for public utilities and services until Greece joins economic and monetary union (EMU).

--The government is preparing to use a freeze on all public utilities and services tariffs until Greece joins EMU as a counterpoise to strict incomes policies for 1998-99. The government hopes the proposal will gain the ground lost in the battle against inflation.

--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou gave notice yesterday of a "second OTE" (Greece telecoms organisation) in reference to efforts to deregulate markets. Papandreou was speaking in Parliament on the issue of a deregulation of the electricity market and of Greece's electricity supplier, DEH.

--The Bank of Greece is putting the final touches to decisions that will substantially contribute towards the deregulation of the currency market in Greece. The changes will mean that individuals will be able to open forex accounts in Greece without restraint and will also lift regulations on tourist exchange.

--The lifting of checks at customs posts on internal borders with the European Union has meant a loss of 200 billion drachmas for Greece. The finance ministry, according to reports, is planning to overcome the obstacles by asking importers for a statutory declaration at the borders which will identify the goods being imported and their destination.

--Agricultural spending sacrificed on the altar of Maastricht? Drastic cutbacks in spending on agriculture are being promoted by the European Union as part of the revision of the common agricultural policy, ahead of the next expansion phase, which will include Central and Eastern European countries.

--A dispute is breaking out between creditors of the troubled ECON and ELVIEMEK companies, both part of the Oikonomidis Group, with a court recently declaring ECON bankrupt despite bank efforts to shore up the company. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
